common_name: Brookfield Delight Dahlia (Compact Orange Single-Flowered Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers 4-6 inches deep, eye up, in full sun once the soil has warmed after the last frost.

directions: Brookfield Delight is a dwarf, bushy single-flowered dahlia bred for massed bedding, producing simple orange blooms with a small open center that bees and other pollinators can reach easily. Its compact habit needs no staking and little pinching, making it a reliable choice for the front of a border or a patio container. Deadhead spent blooms regularly to keep new buds forming through the season. This variety holds the RHS Award of Garden Merit for its dependable garden performance.

planting.note: Plant tubers 4-6 inches deep, eye up, in full sun once the soil has warmed after the last frost.

directions: Dovegrove is a tall, free-flowering single dahlia with broad, flat red petals giving an open daisy-like bloom on wiry stems held well above the foliage. Because it reaches around a yard in height on a relatively narrow spread, stake plants at planting time to keep the slender stems from toppling in wind and rain. Pinch the main shoot while young to encourage side branching and a longer succession of flowers. Dovegrove carries the RHS Award of Garden Merit, reflecting decades of reliable performance in UK trial gardens.

common_name: Happy Days Purple Dahlia (Dwarf Violet-Purple Single-Flowered Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers 4-6 inches deep, eye up, in full sun once the soil has warmed after the last frost.

directions: Happy Days Purple is a low, mounding single-flowered dahlia bred for bedding displays, its violet-purple ray florets forming a flat ring around a contrasting center. At well under knee height it stays tidy without pinching or staking, making it a dependable choice for edging, window boxes, and other small-space plantings. Water regularly through summer to keep the compact plants flowering continuously into fall. It holds the RHS Award of Garden Merit, a mark given only to dahlias that perform consistently across multiple trial seasons.

common_name: Harvest Samantha Dahlia (Deep Pink Lilliput Single Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers 4-6 inches deep, eye up, in full sun once the soil has warmed after the last frost.

directions: Harvest Samantha belongs to the lilliput class of single dahlias, producing masses of small, deep-pink blooms only an inch or two across on a bushy plant that flowers more heavily than most larger-flowered types. The sheer number of small flowers makes it useful for edging and cutting, even though each individual bloom is modest in size. Shear lightly in midsummer if growth becomes leggy to encourage fresh flushes of bloom. Its RHS Award of Garden Merit recognizes its unusually free-flowering habit for the lilliput group.

planting.note: Plant tubers 4-6 inches deep, eye up, in full sun once the soil has warmed after the last frost.

directions: Knockout is a vigorous, large-flowered single dahlia with broad golden-yellow petals washed in orange toward the base, producing bold daisy-form blooms on a sturdy plant whose spread matches its height, unusual for a single-flowered type. Because it grows as wide as it is tall, give it generous spacing and stake the main stems in exposed sites. Deadhead regularly, since removing spent flowers on single types does much more to extend bloom than on fuller double forms. Knockout's RHS Award of Garden Merit reflects its reliability as a tall border single despite the simplicity of its flower form.

common_name: Marie Schnugg Dahlia (Red and Yellow Single Orchid-Flowered Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers 4-6 inches deep, eye up, in full sun once the soil has warmed after the last frost.

directions: Marie Schnugg is a single orchid-type dahlia, its narrow, slightly incurved red petals edged in yellow giving each bloom a star-like outline rather than the flat profile of a standard single. It holds the RHS Award of Garden Merit for its long track record of dependable flowering in British trial beds. Pinch young plants to build a bushier framework of flowering stems, and lift and store tubers over winter outside the mildest zones.

common_name: Twyning's Revel Dahlia (Tall Deep Pink Single Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers 4-6 inches deep, eye up, in full sun once the soil has warmed after the last frost.

directions: Twyning's Revel is a tall single dahlia carrying deep pink flowers on stems that can reach four feet, sharing its series name with the dark-leaved 'Twyning's After Eight,' also a real AGM single. Its height and spread rival many decorative and cactus dahlias, so stake plants early and allow full spacing. Pinch young growth to encourage branching and a longer season of bloom. It holds the RHS Award of Garden Merit for consistent garden performance.
